items.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that a new air-defence system shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper over the Strait of Hormuz, which they called the 58th downed since the war began. Later the same day they claimed an MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island. The US military did not comment immediately. The claims follow tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes earlier in the week.
items.notes: Drone claims come from IRGC via state broadcaster IRIB and have not been independently confirmed. The Washington Post reported in August that the US had lost 45 MQ-9s in Iran operations.

items.text: Bahrain's Defence Force said its air defences intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks overnight into Nov 22 with no injuries, and that an Iranian strike on Saturday hit a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire. Smoke was seen over Sitra Island, home to a Bapco refinery. Iran's Fars agency said the Revolutionary Guards attacked two US bases in Bahrain. Gulf News also reports that Iran is preparing 14 oil tankers to try to run the US naval blockade of its ports, which could lead to a confrontation with US warships.
items.notes: The attacks on US bases are Iran's claim (Fars). The 14-tanker plan is described as a report and its sourcing is not given. No US statement was found.

items.text: On Friday the Treasury sanctioned four Iranians it called 'oil trustees': Mohammad Javad Bavand, Majid Taj, Mohammad Hossein Servati and Mojtaba Arabnejad. It accuses them of handling illicit oil revenue to get around sanctions and the US naval blockade. On the same day Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said seven conditions, including an end to the war and the lifting of sanctions and the blockade, must be met before Hormuz reopens. He also ruled out sending Iran's 60% enriched uranium abroad.
items.notes: The Treasury press release itself was not opened, so names come from the Al Jazeera/Reuters report. Araghchi's remarks were given to the state-owned Iran newspaper (Reuters via Oman Observer). He said Iran wants guarantees of US seriousness and still sees 'a fair solution' as possible.

items.text: The Washington Post reported on Nov 20, citing US officials, that War Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a classified memo restricting US military cooperation with Canada. The Post did not see the memo, and it is unclear which programmes are affected. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the guidance does not touch intelligence cooperation, NORAD or NATO work. Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said NATO 'just can't be our only way of working together'.
items.notes: The Post's report relies on unnamed officials, one of whom said Ottawa would see it as a 'slap in the face'. A Five Eyes official told the Post that US information-sharing has shrunk across several channels over the past year. Trump said of Canada: 'they feel emboldened. We can't let them feel that way anymore.' Only the Newsmax wire rewrite was read, not the Post original.

items.text: On Saturday morning, masked plainclothes federal officers detained two people on the jet bridge of an Alaska Airlines flight from Seattle-Tacoma airport to Los Angeles. DHS said the target was Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, whom it accuses of overstaying a visa, and that Sofia Hernandez Mejia will be charged with assaulting an officer. Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson called the video 'horrific and chilling'. The Port of Seattle said it was outraged and had no knowledge of the operation, and Alaska Airlines said it got no advance notice.
items.notes: DHS says other travellers obstructed officers and one threw coffee. A witness quoted by KUOW describes a girl screaming on the floor while her father was taken out, and says a pilot walked off the flight. KUOW had not independently confirmed the agents were ICE, but DHS described the operation to ABC. At least two other Sea-Tac arrests since August (KING 5).

items.text: US District Judge Jennifer Rochon in New York declined to issue a long-term ban on the administration's taxpayer-funded TV ads. She ruled that Common Cause and other plaintiffs had not shown imminent, irreparable harm now that the Nov 3 midterms are over. The ads, which began airing in September, were paid for at least partly through a $20 million DHS contract, and some featured the president. A separate DNC suit in Washington is still pending, with a temporary restraining order there expiring next week.
items.notes: Plaintiffs call the ads illegal propaganda; the White House calls them public service announcements. Earlier TROs in October had pulled the ads before the election.

items.text: At a hearing on Nov 20, US District Judge Myong Joun signalled he is willing to block the administration's freeze on more than 100,000 green-card applications from refugees admitted under President Biden. He questioned whether processing can be halted indefinitely and said he was 'struggling' to understand why USCIS cut the window to appeal status terminations from 30 days to 10. The shorter appeal window is already paused while he considers the merits. Refugee groups argue the freeze and re-vetting exceed the Refugee Act of 1980.
items.notes: Only source read is a low-credibility outlet relaying Reuters, so confirm with Reuters before relying on details. Plaintiffs say the shorter appeal window could affect 186,000 more applications.

items.text: The Labor Department's final rule on independent contractor status, announced on Nov 19, is scheduled for Federal Register publication on Nov 23 (doc. 2026-23777). It rescinds the 2024 rule and returns to a framework close to the 2021 one, with two core factors: control over the work and the chance of profit or loss. Skill, permanence and integration remain secondary factors, and new examples cover platform workers, truck drivers and farm labour contractors. The rule takes effect 60 days after publication, applies under the FLSA, FMLA and MSPA, and leaves stricter state ABC tests in place.
items.notes: The Nov 23 publication date comes from the Federal Register URL found in search; the page itself could not be opened. SHRM backs the rule. Proskauer (Natl Law Review, Nov 21) notes the DOL dropped a proposal that a control finding alone could settle classification. No worker-advocate reaction was found.

items.text: In a 'Saturday in America' interview with Kayleigh McEnany on Fox News, Trump called likely Speaker Hakeem Jeffries a 'reasonable guy' and said he might 'start with vetoes just to set the stage'. He named healthcare, the debt ceiling and a possible 10% cap on credit-card interest as areas for compromise. Asked about 2028, he said JD Vance and Marco Rubio are both 'very, very popular' but warned of 'some surprises'.
items.notes: Largely repeats his Nov 20 news-conference line. New items are the credit-card cap and the 2028 comments. Only Fox coverage was found. Separately, Democratic Reps. Ansari and Khanna urged blocking Iran offensive funding in the next spending bill (Al Jazeera).

items.text: Levent Alpöge, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, said on Nov 20 that he had found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis with help from Claude. He published it as about 17 million lines of Lean formal-proof code plus a four-page summary. The Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem as unsolved, and its president Martin Bridson said assessing it will take time. Rutgers mathematician Alex Kontorovich said the Lean code checks but he does not yet fully understand it.
items.thread: Anthropic IPO and AI market valuations
items.notes: Unverified claim. Anthropic did not comment to AP. Not to be confused with Anthropic's earlier, more limited Claude result on the zeta function's zeros, which Scientific American stressed was not a proof of the hypothesis.

items.text: On Nov 20 the FDA posted two nationwide recalls. Breckenridge Pharmaceutical is recalling one lot (PK25110035) of propranolol ER 60 mg capsules for possible metal contamination that could cut soft tissue in the digestive tract; it was shipped Oct 26–Nov 4. Greenwich Rx, a Texas compounding pharmacy, is recalling compounded sterile products dispensed Aug 10–Sep 21 over a lack of sterility assurance found after an FDA inspection. Neither company reports adverse events.
items.notes: These are company announcements posted by the FDA.

items.text: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte visited Warsaw on Saturday and said NATO would defend every centimetre of Polish territory. He called the Nov 20 incursion of Russian objects dangerous, said it was still being investigated and that he could not guarantee it would not happen again. He said he had spoken with the prime minister and the president. Asked about US bases, he said that was a matter between Poland and the US, which is reviewing its force posture in Europe. Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz said he would ask Rutte for more Eastern Sentry assets, including an extra AWACS aircraft.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: Rutte made no confirmed new deployment decision; he said SACEUR would assess threats and could adjust. The AWACS request is Kosiniak-Kamysz's, not an approved measure.

items.text: Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski told RMF FM that Poland will present concrete proposals to strengthen eastern-flank air defence at an extraordinary North Atlantic Council meeting in Brussels on Monday (Nov 23), where he will represent Poland. He said Poland will not request Article 4 consultations, citing ongoing NATO activity such as Eastern Sentry, and does not expect a joint communiqué. Kosiniak-Kamysz said Poland would soon receive NATO support to strengthen protection of its eastern border. Foreign Minister Sikorski said Poland would convey its 'extreme dissatisfaction' to Russia once hard facts are confirmed.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: Zalewski declined to detail the proposals publicly. Sikorski quote via Dziennik.pl/PAP: https://wiadomosci.dziennik.pl/polityka/artykuly/11349681,naruszenie-polskiej-przestrzeni-powietrznej-sikorski-bedziemy-komunikowac-nasze-ekstremalne-niezadowolenie.html

items.text: Lublin District Prosecutor Andrzej Boroń confirmed that the object that fell at Nowy Lipowiec was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile and said it was manufactured in the fourth quarter of this year. Serial numbers on recovered parts identify the factory, which was not named. Investigators believe the missile exploded in the air, scattering debris over several hectares; the engine and steering components were recovered. Site work at Rudnik nad Sanem is finished, while work at Mołodycz (Podkarpackie), where an object fell about 280 m from an empty summer house, was to resume on Sunday. Prosecutors said only written expert opinions will be binding.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: Interia (Aleksandra Czurczak) carries the same prosecutor quotes and notes the crater was smaller than at Tarnawa-Kolonia (30 July).

items.text: The opposition attacked the government over the timing of warnings during the Nov 20 incursion. PiS's Rafał Bochenek asked whether the government had overslept, Mariusz Błaszczak demanded to know why the objects were not shot down and where the Patriot launchers are, and Konfederacja MPs said Polish airspace was 'like a sieve'. Interior Minister Kierwiński said the response was immediate and accused part of the opposition of political hatred; the ministry's spokeswoman called some witness accounts disinformation. The Podkarpackie voivode said preliminary analysis showed sirens sounded before a resident's 112 call.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: Framing differs: centrist Interia sets the opposition criticism against the government timeline. Right-libertarian nczas.info gives prominence to a Rudnik nad Sanem resident (via Polsat News) and the Aleksandrów wójt, who say alerts came after the blast, and treats official rebuttals sceptically. Witness accounts are uncorroborated.

items.text: The dispute between the Foreign Ministry and the President's Chancellery over ambassadors escalated. Marcin Przydacz, head of the President's International Policy Bureau, accused Radosław Sikorski of escalating the conflict by sending agrément requests for new ambassadors to more than a dozen capitals without the President's consent, and said those candidates would not get letters of credence. Sikorski told TVP Info this was 'absurd', saying the President signs nominations but cannot appoint whoever he wants and that Poland does not have a presidential system. According to RMF24, 46 appointments and 38 recalls are awaiting the President's signature.
items.notes: Sikorski said candidates for China, Romania and the UN (where ambassadors resigned in Oct–Nov) will go first to the PM and the Diplomatic Service Council. Przydacz cites the President's constitutional power to appoint envoys.

items.text: Warsaw Mayor Rafał Trzaskowski rejected criticism from Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, who called him hypocritical over his condemnation of 'Slava UPA' graffiti on two Warsaw monuments in early November. Trzaskowski said he would not take lessons on memory from a state that lied about Katyń and is bombing Ukrainian cities. He said Poland removes Soviet propaganda symbols but protects soldiers' graves, and noted that Russian missiles had fallen in Poland the same morning.

In an SW Research poll for Rzeczpospolita (800 internet users, Nov 17–18), 23.8% named President Karol Nawrocki as leader of the Polish right, ahead of Jarosław Kaczyński at 19%. Krzysztof Bosak had 7.3%, Sławomir Mentzen 6.7%, Grzegorz Braun 5% and Mateusz Morawiecki 4%; 33.5% had no opinion.
items.notes: Online panel, small sample.

items.text: Rituals Cosmetics Poland became the latest company to pull advertising from the right-wing TV Republika; its spots will stop from December. It follows RTV Euro AGD, Mastercard and Chery. The withdrawals began after a controversial broadcast by the channel's head, Tomasz Sakiewicz, following the Nov 7 Kraków attack. Sakiewicz responded by calling on viewers to boycott those companies.
items.notes: TV Republika itself frames the withdrawals as political pressure and has called for boycotts (see tvrepublika.pl on RTV Euro AGD).

items.text: Wrocław police detained a 42-year-old man from Wałbrzych county and charged him with criminal threats against KO MP Anna Sobolak. He allegedly sent messages to her private phone, including 'you are for shooting'. He faces up to three years in prison and is under police supervision with a contact ban.

A magnitude 3.2 tremor at the 900-metre level of the Murcki-Staszic coal mine was felt early on Saturday in Katowice, Chorzów, Mysłowice, Świętochłowice, Czeladź and Sosnowiec. No damage or injuries were reported. PGG spokeswoman Ewa Grudniok said there was no threat to the crew and the workings would be inspected.

Poland beat Sweden 3–2 in a Billie Jean King Cup play-off in Włocławek, playing without Iga Świątek and other leading players. Linda Klimovicova won the deciding singles against Caijsa Hennemann 4–6, 6–4, 6–3. The win gives Poland a chance in April 2027 to qualify for the Finals.

Wisła Kraków's Ekstraklasa match at Radomiak Radom kicked off 30 minutes late, at 20:45, and ended 0:0. Overnight vandals had cut the glass doors of an emergency exit in the away sector, and the Mazovian voivode closed that sector at the Radom police commander's request. Wisła president Jarosław Królewski said the team would not play unless its roughly 600-700 travelling fans were let in. Police then withdrew their negative assessment, the voivode lifted the closure, and Wisła fans entered late in the first half. Voivode Mariusz Frankowski asked PZPN and Ekstraklasa SA for clear standards so the decision does not fall on police and state bodies.
items.notes: Sportowe Fakty (Rafał Szymański) gives the full sequence: police opened an inquiry into the vandalism and secured CCTV. Radomiak said the doors had been replaced and had a technical opinion. LoveKraków reported Radomiak could face fines of up to about 1m zł for refusing away fans. After the match Królewski thanked Ekstraklasa, PZPN and Radomiak and called the vandals 'imbeciles' (meczyki.pl). The voivode's statement on X was reported by transfery.info. No disciplinary proceedings reported yet.

items.text: Cracovia beat Jagiellonia Białystok 3:1 at home in round 15 of the Ekstraklasa, in Aleksandar Vuković's first match as coach. The goals came from Lasse Nordås, Karol Knap and Dominik Piła, with Nik Prelec replying for Jagiellonia. The win lifts Cracovia to 12th with 15 points, out of the relegation zone. It comes a day after the club announced a transitional management board.
items.notes: Vuković was appointed on 11 November with a contract to 2028 (Radio Kraków). The scorers for the third Cracovia goal and the Jagiellonia goal come from CANAL+ SPORT posts embedded in the iGol report.

items.text: A man riding an electric bicycle died after a crash shortly after 14:00 on Saturday near the junction of Tyniecka and Jemiołowa streets. According to preliminary police findings, he lost control while heading towards the centre and hit a metal bridge barrier, suffering serious head injuries. He died in hospital. Police spokeswoman Iwona Szelichiewicz said the e-bike will be examined, and police do not rule out that it did not meet legal requirements.
items.notes: Police information relayed by Radio Kraków. An accident reconstruction expert's opinion is expected to establish the cause.

items.text: Bus operators UniBus and Inter are ending their express Katowice–Kraków coach service, with the last run on 30 November 2026, LoveKraków reports. Both cite the economic situation and falling passenger numbers. The route started in 2009 and once ran as often as every 15 minutes, but it has lost passengers to rail since the Silesia–Małopolska line was modernised.
items.notes: Based on statements from both carriers quoted by LoveKraków (editorial byline).

items.text: About 200 people in folk costume walked in a wedding procession from St Anthony's church in Bronowice to the Rydlówka Museum, where the traditional straw 'chochoł' was set up. The event marks 126 years since the wedding of Lucjan Rydel and Jadwiga Mikołajczykówna, which inspired Wyspiański's 'Wesele'. The custom dates from 1969, when the museum opened.

The seventh 'Przedświąteczny karp dla Krakowa' gives out free carp and cabbage with peas at six places: Nowohuckie Centrum Kultury (30 Nov), pl. Inwalidów (2 Dec), pl. Wolnica (4 Dec), Rynek Podgórski (7 Dec), Rondo Mogilskie (9 Dec) and Rynek Główny (11 Dec). Serving runs from 16:00, with about 1,500 portions per location. It is aimed mainly at seniors and people in difficulty and is funded by the owners of a fish farm, Dolina Będkowska.
items.notes: Published 20 Nov 13:30, after the previous run's sources were checked; not in recent log.

items.text: Part of ul. Kościuszkowców near Zakopiańska closes to cars from 23 November for about a week while the surface and drainage are repaired. Drivers are sent via Niemcewicza, Montwiłła-Mireckiego, Zbrojarzy and Zakopiańska, and parking is banned on all of Niemcewicza and part of Zbrojarzy. Pedestrians can pass on a marked route.
items.notes: Based on City Hall (UMK) information relayed by the outlets.

items.text: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik spoke on Nov 21 at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila, in a session chaired by Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. Speaking in Urdu, he quoted Ghalib and used the fort's history (Humayun, then Sher Shah Suri) to argue that dialogue needs distinct identities. ThePrint reports he said single incidents should not dominate relations and called for a transparent mechanism for sharing evidence on cross-border terrorism. He did not mention the Indus Waters Treaty. No bilateral meeting with Indian officials was reported. India let him visit the Taj Mahal but turned down a request to visit Nizamuddin Dargah on security grounds.
items.notes: The PTI version (Telangana Today, The Federal) stresses the history and culture passages and quotes Malik saying everything was happening 'in a multilateral context'. ThePrint also reports the call for evidence-sharing on terrorism. In earlier ThePrint reporting (Vrinda Tulsian, Nov 21), Malik told reporters 'all of our relationships will improve'. The Taj/Nizamuddin detail comes from ThePrint only.

items.text: Polling in Ladakh's first panchayat and municipal elections since it became a Union Territory ended peacefully at 5 pm on Nov 21, PTI reports. Turnout was 70.03% for sarpanch posts and 52.4% in the Leh and Kargil municipal polls; the Lieutenant Governor gave 73.60% for panch posts. Helicopters flew polling teams to three snowbound stations in Zanskar. The Leh Apex Body says several villages boycotted the vote over hill-council delimitation and moved polling stations, and it wants the Dec 4 LAHDC polls put off. No date for results was reported.
items.outlet: PTI (via Free Press Journal); IBTimes India
items.thread: Ladakh statehood protests and council polls
items.notes: Turnout figures changed during the day. UNI's early count was 48.21% panchayat and 40.57% municipal; IBTimes had 62.48% panch and 60.18% sarpanch, with Kargil MC at 62.04% and Leh MC at 33.70% at 2 pm. The final figures above are PTI's. The boycott is the Leh Apex Body's claim.

items.text: PM Modi opened Nitish Setu over the Ganga in Vaishali on Nov 21. It links Kachchi Dargah (Patna) with Raghopur and Bidupur. The main bridge is 9.76 km long, or 19.76 km with approaches, and L&T and Daewoo E&C built it. During the visit 227 projects worth over ₹34,000 crore were opened or had foundations laid. In his speech Modi praised Nitish Kumar and CM Samrat Choudhary, accused Congress of 'looting votes' of the poor and criticised past RJD governments. Earlier he went to IIT Kharagpur's platinum jubilee, and later to the National Skills Convocation in Lucknow.
items.notes: ETV Bharat calls it India's longest river bridge, the government's description. The bridge's own cost was not given separately.

items.text: Brickwork Ratings forecast real GDP growth of about 7% for FY27 in a report released on Nov 21. It expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and then hold for a long period, because inflation is persistent. October CPI inflation was 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% upper limit. Brickwork sees CPI peaking at 5.8–6.1% in Q3 and averaging 5.2% for the year.
items.notes: A rating agency's forecast, not an official one.

items.text: Drone Federation India told defence officials in a Nov 20 representation that 689 Government e-Marketplace tenders from March 2021 to Nov 19, 2026 named Chinese drones or parts. The Army issued 580 of them (84%), including 328 of 355 so far in 2026. According to the federation, 104 of this year's Army tenders came after the Army's AASHVAST lab for screening Chinese components opened in August. It wants Chinese components barred from military drones and country-of-origin traceability made mandatory. No government response was reported.
items.notes: The figures are the industry body's own count, as reported by ThePrint.

items.text: Police complaints have been filed in Karnataka against author Ravi Hanj and publisher Vishweshwara Bhat over the 600-page book 'Basava Mantapa', which critics say distorts Basavanna's teachings, ThePrint reports. Protesters tore and burned pages. CM D.K. Shivakumar said on social media that the government is seizing copies and 'will not remain silent'. Hanj has apologised and says his views were misinterpreted. B.S. Yediyurappa also condemned remarks disparaging Basavanna.
items.notes: ThePrint's homepage headline later said Hanj had been arrested, but the article text we read (12:57 IST) reports only complaints. Treat the arrest as unconfirmed. No formal seizure order has been published.

items.text: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah was due in New Delhi on Nov 22 for a two-day visit at Modi's invitation, his first bilateral trip abroad. According to the Kathmandu Post, the programme includes a one-on-one meeting with Modi, delegation talks and a business event on Nov 23. Nepal wants new air entry routes, especially via Mahendranagar and Bhairahawa, and India is expected to offer an economic package. Possible announcements include an Ayodhya–Janakpur rail link and a Bhairahawa integrated check post. The paper expects little progress on the boundary dispute, the suspended Gorkha recruitment or Pancheshwar.
items.notes: This is a preview: the visit was scheduled for that day. Amar Ujala's Nov 22 headlines list the visit as 'today'.

items.text: Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah was scheduled to launch four Arunachal Pradesh programmes worth over ₹5,610 crore on Nov 22. They cover school education, state power, rural roads, and 199 Vibrant Villages projects in 11 border districts. He was also due to open the NDRF 12th Battalion campus at Hollongi and release a Cooperation Vision 2047 document.
items.notes: Based on a preview; completion not confirmed.

items.text: Amar Ujala's list of events for Nov 22 says air-raid and blackout mock drills are planned in all districts of Uttar Pradesh. We could not open the full article, so the time and organiser are not known.
items.notes: Only the headline was seen; the site blocks automated reading.

items.text: An Amar Ujala piece on Nov 22 says UP CM Yogi Adityanath's mother has died. It discusses questions about a monk's duty to his mother, arguing that a sannyasi can renounce everything except his mother. We could not open the article, so the date and circumstances of her death are not confirmed here.
items.notes: Only the headline and URL were seen. Check details before using.

items.text: According to an Amar Ujala headline, the BJP has reshuffled its OBC Morcha, appointing seven vice-presidents and three general secretaries. Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has been given a role.
items.notes: Only the headline was seen. The link to UP 2027 is our inference.

items.text: The clerk of the US District Court for the Southern District of New York sent summonses by FedEx on Friday, Nov 20, to three New Delhi courts (Patiala House, Tis Hazari and Dwarka). The summonses are addressed to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel in Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's civil damages suit. Judge Katherine Polk Failla ordered them issued on Nov 13. The court allowed this route under Article 19 of the Hague Service Convention and India's Code of Civil Procedure after service through India's central authority was refused; an earlier attempt via a State Department diplomatic note also failed. India's MEA had called the suits frivolous on Nov 10 and said service must go through the Law Ministry.
items.notes: PTC News (Nov 21) cites no wire service. Kashmir Media Service (Pakistan-linked, Nov 22) gives the same details. Deccan Herald also ran the story but its page would not load. No Indian government reaction to the dispatch itself was found. Whether service by post to Indian courts will be accepted is unclear.

items.text: Speaking to reporters at the White House on Nov 20, President Trump pointed to India as an example in his attack on the Federal Reserve. He said India has low interest rates and about 7% GDP growth, and claimed the US could grow 14–20% with similar rates. He did not mention trade or tariffs with India in the remarks reported.
items.notes: Indian outlets (The Federal, India TV, Organiser, Amar Ujala in Hindi) presented it as praise for India. The comment was aimed at the Fed, not at India policy. The 14–20% growth claim is Trump's own.

items.text: A Bloomberg report, republished by Business Standard on Nov 21, describes skilled foreign workers, many of them Indian H-1B holders, leaving the US because of visa delays, new fees and tighter green-card rules. It says a separate $103,000 fee now applies to new H-1B applications after a court blocked the 2025 $100,000 payment. It also says IBM is ending visa sponsorship for most jobs in its largest division. The report adds that the number of new international students fell an estimated 15% this autumn and that Optional Practical Training participation fell 6%.
items.notes: This is a feature, not a new policy step. The $103,000 fee and the IBM change come from Bloomberg's own reporting (an internal IBM document). Neither was checked against an official source here.

items.text: PEJ management board president Marek Woszczyk told Dow Jones Newswires that signing the roughly $50bn EPC contract with Westinghouse and Bechtel by the end of Q1 2027 now looks most likely. The parties had hoped to sign by the end of 2026. He said the delay would not affect the plan to start the three AP1000 reactors in 2036–2038. This differs from Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka's Nov 20 statement that the contract should be signed before the end of 2026.
items.outlet: The Jerusalem Post (citing Dow Jones Newswires / WSJ)
items.notes: Late catch: the interview was published on Nov 19, before this window, and had not been logged. It contradicts the minister's end-2026 timing logged in E-261121-65. The original WSJ/Dow Jones piece is paywalled; this account comes from JPost and Newsquawk.

items.text: Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk met US Under Secretary of State for Arms Control and International Security Thomas DiNanno in Washington. They discussed a permanent US base in Poland, Poland's planned purchase of Tomahawk cruise missiles, joint industrial projects and the eastern flank. Tomczyk wrote on X that the State Department will support Poland's efforts. Congress must still approve any Tomahawk sale.
items.notes: Late catch from Nov 19, not logged before. The only source is the Polish side's account (Tomczyk's X post via RMF24/PAP). No State Department readout was found.
